title: Spengler wins Norisring Race 1 as BMW takes five of the top six
dek: Bruno Spengler won DTM Race 1 at the Norisring for BMW Team RBM, 4.385 seconds clear of pole-sitter Maxime Martin, while Mattias Ekström's third place put the Audi driver top of the standings.

chapters.title: A new leader, a hungry BMW and a rallycross sacrifice
text: The DTM reached the Norisring for the fourth round of 2017 with a new man at the top of the table. René Rast had started both Hungaroring races from pole two weeks earlier. In Race 1 the Audi Sport Team Rosberg driver was held to sixth, as Paul di Resta won for Mercedes from 13th on the grid with Timo Glock second for BMW; in Race 2 Rast converted pole into victory, ahead of Mattias Ekström. That was enough to put him one point ahead of Lucas Auer, who had won two of the first six races but left Hungary with nothing, twelfth in the first race and a retirement in the second.

The first six races had gone to only four drivers, Auer and Jamie Green twice each, with di Resta and Rast one apiece, and none of them to BMW. The Norisring offered the Munich marque a chance: BMW was running at 1,117.5 kilograms while Audi and Mercedes were at 1,122.5, which made the M4 DTM the lightest car in the field. The 2.3-kilometre track in Nuremberg is the shortest on the calendar and its only street circuit, built from long straights and a handful of heavy braking zones, and in practice the gaps were as small as ever. Auer had been fastest in Saturday morning's second practice.

Audi had a driver in two minds. Ekström had to choose between this weekend and a round of the World Rallycross Championship that fell on the same dates, and Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass decided that the Swede would race in the DTM. He arrived as one of the form drivers: second at the Hungaroring in Race 2, and eight points behind Rast in the table.

chapters.title: Martin snatches pole on the last lap
text: Qualifying was held in the dry, under dark clouds and with only a few spots of rain in the air, at roughly 16 degrees. Auer led after the first runs, but the order was reshuffled on the second set of tyres: Tom Blomqvist went top, Bruno Spengler and then Rast followed him, and Maxime Martin moved up to second. The chequered flag was already out when Martin crossed the line in his BMW Team RBM M4 with a 47.472 that beat Rast by five thousandths of a second.

BMW filled three of the first four places, with Spengler third (0.021 seconds off) and Blomqvist fourth (0.055). Auer took fifth, 0.112 down, and was the only Mercedes in the top ten; Mattias Ekström was sixth, Marco Wittmann seventh and Timo Glock eighth, ahead of Audi's Jamie Green and Nico Müller. Robert Wickens, the next Mercedes, was eleventh, Gary Paffett thirteenth, and Loïc Duval qualified last, 0.651 seconds behind the pole time.

The points on offer made the gaps matter: three for pole, two for second and one for third place, so Rast's second place stretched his lead over Auer to three. He said he was delighted with it, though a pole position would have been nice, and he expected a tight race because the circuit is not hard on tyres.

chapters.title: Rain, two formation laps and a lap-one scramble
text: A heavy shower soaked the track shortly before the start. The sun returned before the lights, but the surface was still wet, so the field lined up on rain tyres and race control ordered two formation laps. Maro Engel spun on one of them. The extra lap cut the race from 55 to 52 minutes plus one lap.

Spengler made the start of the weekend. From the second row he was past Martin and Rast and in front well before the first braking zone, while the pole-sitter got away slowly and dropped back. Ekström flew from the third row to second. At the hairpin, Auer ran wide and in the contact that followed Wickens was damaged against the wall; Wickens stopped his Mercedes on the track without completing a lap, and Auer limped to the pits, where his race ended after one.
On lap nine Martin dived inside Ekström at the hairpin to take second, with Spengler by then five to six seconds clear. From about lap ten a dry line began to appear.

chapters.title: Drive-throughs reshuffle the midfield
text: The first cars came in for slicks around lap 18, with Green among them, and the rest followed over the next few laps. Martin and Ekström came in together, and Spengler a lap later. Rast, who had been running fourth, crossed the yellow line at the pit exit, and the drive-through penalty that followed dropped him to twelfth at the flag.

Spengler struggled for grip on slicks on the still-damp track and Martin was soon on his tail, with Ekström closing up to make it a three-car train. Spengler found a rhythm again within a lap or two and pulled clear. The track dried only on the racing line, which made passing in the midfield difficult and kept the order there largely unchanged.

The other penalty went to Mike Rockenfeller, who spun Edoardo Mortara round at the hairpin while the Mercedes driver was running in the leading group. Rockenfeller served a drive-through, and Mortara could recover only to eighth.

chapters.title: Spengler wins by 4.385 seconds as Martin holds off Ekström
text: On slicks Martin was the quicker of the two BMWs for a time and got right behind Spengler, but he could not find a way past and lost touch in the final third of the race. Behind him Ekström kept up the pressure. With six laps left he slipstreamed Martin down to the first corner, moved to the inside and then ran wide with understeer mid-corner, which let Martin back ahead. Ekström finished 0.391 seconds behind Martin and said he did not risk everything afterwards, to be sure of the points for third.

Spengler took the flag 4.385 seconds clear for his first DTM win since 2013 and BMW's first of 2017, and said the start had been the key. It was also the first BMW win at the Norisring since 1992. Wittmann, Glock and Blomqvist took fourth to sixth, Blomqvist setting the fastest lap, so BMW had five of the top six. Green was seventh, Mortara eighth and Müller ninth, and Gary Paffett took the last point from di Resta.

Ekström's 15 points made him the new leader on 77, five ahead of Rast, who finished without points on 72 after his penalty. Mercedes had lost two cars on the first lap and had Mortara as its best finisher.

facts.v: Bruno Spengler won Race 1 over 61 laps for his first DTM victory in four years, and BMW's first of the 2017 season.
